value: DIRECTIONAL AUDIT OF THE WHOLE LAW CORPUS: 17 of 17 checked directional claims CONFIRMED against target opcodes; ZERO new backwards laws found. Scope and method. The corpus holds 136 law records (gdlmem laws --full 1 --limit 1000; note the DEFAULT LIMIT IS 100, so an unlimited enumeration is required or 36 laws are silently invisible - that alone is worth knowing). Of these, 31 assert a codegen DIRECTION. 23 are DIRECTIONALLY CHECKABLE (they pair a target-side verb with named opcodes, so fnasm can adjudicate them); 8 assert a direction but name fewer than two opcodes and are flagged UNVERIFIABLE-AS-WRITTEN below. 17 checkable laws were verified instruction-for-instruction at their origin functions this pass. VERDICT COUNTS: CONFIRMED 17, BACKWARDS 0 (new), UNVERIFIABLE-AS-WRITTEN 8, PARTIAL/IMPRECISE 1, not-reached 5. CONFIRMED, each with the verifying opcodes: (1) recomputed-index-array-form-safe.v2 at enemy.c::do_enemies - target 0x174 `add r3,r31,r5` + 0x180 `stfs f0,64(r3)`, and NO stfsx anywhere in the target, so v2's correction of v1 is itself correct. (2) zero-remat-choice-differs-between-identical-sibling-loops at critter.c::ProcessCritter - target 0xb4 `mr r30,r29` and 0x23c `li r30,0`, the two sibling preheaders genuinely disagreeing, which is the law's whole proof. (3) repeated-fp-pool-literal-first-load-is-position-invariant at pb_window.c::pbProjCalc - target issues `lfs f1,@lbl_80349018` at exactly 0x68 as claimed, with 0x28 holding an unrelated lwz. (4) two-use-preoffset-pointer-keeps-add-then-addi at sfx.c::StartMagicHealFX - target 0xa0-0xac is `mulli r0,r30,240; add r27,r31,r0; lwz r3,2996(r27); addi r27,r27,2976`, the recited sequence verbatim. (5) loop-exit-goto-pair-is-not-source-reachable at audio.c::AudioLoadPart - target 0x70 `bge ->78` then 0x74 `b ->88`, the unfused pair at the stated offsets. (6) recomputed-base-update-load-fuses-lwzu at mb_font.c::MBRenderText - target 0xd8 `add r31,r19,r17` + 0xdc `lwzu r3,4300(r31)`. (7) walked-base-symbol-identity at world.c::FindWorldAnimNode - target relocates against lbl_8028C9A8 (ADDR16_HA 0x1c / LO 0x30), NOT gWorldInfo, exactly as claimed. (8) live-zero-copy-vs-remat-is-allocator-not-source - BOTH directions confirmed: audio.c::AudioUnloadPart target +0x24 emits the COPY `addi r29,r31,0`, while dcsdrv.c::dcsHandleRequest target emits the REMAT `li r28,0`, so the law's bidirectionality claim (its central argument for source-unreachability) holds. (9) single-base-relocation-refutes-symbol-separation - shop.c::write_shop_menu target has exactly ONE @lbl_802897D0 HA/LO pair (0x4/0x38) then `addi ...,6480/5456/4432/336` at 0x128-0x134; options.c::show_optmenu has exactly ONE @lbl_8011DD20 pair and reaches +216/+220/+224 off r27 by immediate displacement with no second symbol. (10) float-clamp-ternary-diamond-vs-negated-guard at newcam.c::DebugCamControlInputs - target 0x1c-0x28 is `fcmpo; ble ->28; b ->2c; fmr f1,f0`, the predicted ternary diamond with an EMPTY true arm whose lone `b` is the target-only branch; the `cror eq,lt,eq` at 0x3d4/0x414 are genuine negated guards elsewhere in the same function, which corroborates rather than refutes the law, since its point is that the guard-vs-ternary choice must be READ OFF the target per site. (11) declaration-initializer-split-controls-entry-schedule at enemy.c::init_enemy - target materializes the gEnemies base at 0x18-0x24, stores `e->type` at 0x34, and only THEN computes 0x38 `slwi r28,r5,2` and 0x40 `lfs f1,@lbl_80346820`, i.e. the initializers really are deferred past the opening store. (12) dead-offset-shadow-removal-needs-isolated-accumulator at tower.c::EnterTower - target does carry the counted-loop form (mtctr at 0x64/0xb0/0xd8/0x114, bdnz at 0x88/0xcc/0xec/0x1a0) that the array-index rewrite lost. (13) cached-base-alias-defeats-rematerialized-index-base at screensaver.c::ScreenSaverUpdateWeap - target repeats `add rX,r30,r28` at least a dozen times (0x50,0x58,0x8c,0xb4,0xb8,0x154,0x158,0x164...) and carries the predicted update forms `lwzu r0,72(r27)`, `lwzu r3,76(r26)`, `stfsu f0,32(r3)`, `lfsu f1,48(r22)`. (14) shared-level-scaled-base-refuses-member-form at tower.c::TowerCheckMessages - target 0x93c `lha r4,0(r6)` + 0x948 `sth r5,0(r6)` share ONE base register for load and store, the shared-address form the law says member form cannot reach. (15) extern-scalar-read-defeats-fp-literal-hoist at sfx.c::ProcessEffects - target prologue 0x44 `lfd f0,@lbl_80348230` + 0x54 `stfd f0,472(r1)` + 0x58 `lfd f0,@lbl_80348248` is the claimed pool-load/stack-store run. (16) s16-field-compare-via-s32-local-kills-extsh at ProcessEffects - PARTICULARLY strong: the target uses BOTH forms on the SAME field 190(r31), `extsh. r6,r3` at 0x518 and `cmpwi r0,0` at 0x79c, which is exactly the per-site discriminator the law prescribes rather than a blanket rule. (17) scalar-field-cache-defeats-call-boundary-reload at ProcessEffects - target carries the in-loop record-form bitmask tests (`rlwinm.` at 0x22c, 0x2f0, 0x2f8, 0x414, 0x4a4, 0x4b0) that a cached-local build would have hoisted. PARTIAL/IMPRECISE (1): f64-pool-literal-substitution-diverges-from-f32 at select.c::serve_blits - the mechanism is right but the recited target run `xoris, stw, add, lwz, mr, lfd, stw, fsub` does not match the actual 0xd8-0xe0 `xoris, lwz, stw`; the opcode ORDER in that law's prose is approximate and should not be pattern-matched literally. A second, smaller imprecision: single-base-relocation says show_optmenu reaches '+216/+228' where the target actually reaches +216/+220/+224 - direction sound, numbers loose. UNVERIFIABLE-AS-WRITTEN (8), flagged for tightening because they assert a direction while naming fewer than two opcodes, so no fnasm read can adjudicate them: arg-constant-switch-arms-defeat-literal-sweep, base-cast-reconstruction-deadstrips-sibling-statics, gCameraState-blob-vs-typed-camera-base, pointer-reassociation-controls-add-operand-order, volatile-pins-the-later-of-two-adjacent-reads, gcb-sflags-relocation-alias, write-site-alias-defeats-reload-parity, store-placement-family. These are not necessarily WRONG - several are almost certainly right - but each should gain the target opcodes and offsets at its origin function when next touched, which is a one-fnasm-call cost. INTERPRETATION, and the reason this audit's null result is still worth its cost. EN2's systemic worry was that real-gated de-fakematch passes might have seeded a class of backwards laws. The audit does NOT support that: the one proven backwards law (recomputed-index v1) appears to be the exception, not the pattern, and its v2 correction verifies clean. What the corpus actually has is a weaker and more tractable defect - directional prose that is right in mechanism but loose in recited opcodes, offsets, and ordering - which misleads pattern-matching more than it misleads reasoning. The v2 record's procedural lesson (read the target opcodes at the cluster before describing any conversion as convergent) evidently did get applied by most law authors; what did not get applied is transcribing those opcodes into the law text precisely enough for a later reader to re-check them cheaply.
